public_body: Board Of Elementary And Secondary Education
overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation in requiring photo ID and sign-in to enter the building for the Board's May 21 meeting, since consistent security enforcement is permissible, and declined to address the non-OML complaints; it encouraged clearer notice of the sign-in policy and reminded the Board of its duty to accommodate the public.

allegations.summary: Board required visitors to show photo ID and sign in to enter the Department offices for its May 21 meeting, allegedly violating the OML.
allegations.key_passage: Consistent enforcement of the policy at a public meeting did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged that enforcing the sign-in policy created an unwelcome, embarrassing atmosphere and that Department staff resisted identifying themselves.
allegations.key_passage: Our office is tasked with enforcement of the Open Meeting Law, which is not implicated by any of these allegations.

allegations.summary: One complainant alleged the sign-in requirement violated her constitutional rights.
allegations.key_passage: Our office is tasked with enforcement of the Open Meeting Law, which is not implicated by any of these allegations.
